karty.priklad: Mae'r gadair esmwyth wrth y lle tân.
karty.priklad_cs: The easy chair is by the fireplace (cadair → [g]adair after y, feminine).
karty.mnemo: cadair (chair) + esmwyth (comfy, smooth): a red easy chair pulled up to the glowing embers.

extra.pozn: plural outside the coursebook; the describing word starts with a vowel, so it doesn't mutate; own example

karty.priklad: Diolch am eich dealltwriaeth.
karty.priklad_cs: Thank you for your understanding.
karty.mnemo: deall (to understand) + -iaeth: the penny drops and a red bulb flashes on in your head.

extra.pozn: deallus = intelligent (L13); own example

karty.priklad: Cafodd y ddyled ei thalu.
karty.priklad_cs: The debt was paid (dyled → [dd]yled after y, feminine; talu → [th]alu after ei = her, because dyled is feminine).
karty.mnemo: In debt: the LED (dy-LED) display shows your bank account glowing in the red.

extra.pozn: mewn dyled = in debt; sentence based on the exercise on p. 134 (y dyled + talu)

karty.priklad: Roedd fflamau'n dod o ffenestri'r ffatri.
karty.priklad_cs: Flames were coming out of the factory windows.
karty.mnemo: From English FLAME: red flames licking up from a bonfire.

extra.pozn: Y Fflamau = name of a band in Robin Radio (p. 142); own example based on the news item on p. 140

karty.priklad: Cafodd ei gwefus hi ei thorri yn y gêm.
karty.priklad_cs: She cut her lip in the game (literally: her lip was cut; torri → [th]orri after ei, because gwefus is feminine).
karty.mnemo: Lips hidden in a GUY'S FUZZ (GWE-FUS) of beard, smeared with strawberry jam.

extra.pozn: gwefus goch = red lip (Robin Radio, p. 142; coch → [g]och after the feminine gwefus); own example

karty.priklad: Does dim diddordeb gyda fi mewn gwleidyddiaeth beth bynnag!
karty.priklad_cs: I'm not interested in politics anyway!
karty.mnemo: gwlad (country) → gwleidydd (politician) + -iaeth: red banners waving at an election rally.

extra.pozn: gwleidydd = politician (L20); sentence from the dialogue on p. 137

sever.priklad: Does gen i ddim diddordeb mewn gwleidyddiaeth beth bynnag!
sever.priklad_cs: I'm not interested in politics anyway! (dim → [dd]im after gen i)
sever.pozn: north: Does gen i ddim instead of Does dim … gyda fi (L6)

karty.priklad: Mae'n anodd cael bwyd a meddyginiaeth i sawl ardal.
karty.priklad_cs: It's hard to get food and medicine to many areas.
karty.mnemo: meddyg (doctor) + -iniaeth: what the doctor gives you – a box with a red cross on it.

extra.pozn: sentence from the news on p. 140

karty.priklad: Cafodd y chwaraewr anaf difrifol yn y gêm.
karty.priklad_cs: The player got a serious injury in the game.
karty.mnemo: anafu (to injure) without the -u: an injured knee under a freezing ice pack.

extra.pozn: anafu = to injure (L4); p. 133: ces i fy anafu yn y gêm ddiwetha; own example

karty.priklad: Gwisga dy gap, mae hi'n oer!
karty.priklad_cs: Put your cap on, it's cold! (cap → [g]ap after dy)
karty.mnemo: From English cap: a blue woolly cap pulled down against the sleet.

extra.pozn: in sport also an international appearance: ennill cap dros Gymru; own example

karty.priklad: Cafodd y cwlwm ei glymu.
karty.priklad_cs: The knot was tied (clymu → [g]lymu after ei = its).
karty.mnemo: COOL 'EM (CWL-WM) down: two ropes frozen solid into a knot.

extra.pozn: plural clymau = the same root as clymu (to tie); cwlwm tafod = tongue-twister; sentence based on the exercise on p. 134 (y cwlwm + clymu)

karty.priklad: Mae drych mawr ar y wal yn y cyntedd.
karty.priklad_cs: There's a big mirror on the wall in the hall.
karty.mnemo: You look (eDRYCH) into the mirror (DRYCH): glass as smooth as a sheet of blue ice.

extra.pozn: own example

karty.cs: extension (to a building); extension (of time, phone)
karty.priklad: Cafodd estyniad ei adeiladu ar gefn y tŷ.
karty.priklad_cs: An extension was built at the back of the house (cefn → [g]efn after ar).
karty.mnemo: estyn (to stretch, to reach) + -iad: the house stretches out – a new extension, white and cold as an ice palace.

extra.pozn: ymestyn = to stretch (L8); also an extension of a deadline or a phone extension; own example

karty.priklad: Mae'r ffoaduriaid yn dysgu Cymraeg mewn dosbarth arbennig.
karty.priklad_cs: The refugees are learning Welsh in a special class.
karty.mnemo: ffoi (to flee) + -adur: someone who has fled – across a frozen border at night.

extra.rod_pozn: grammatically masculine even for a woman
extra.pozn: based on the video Dosbarth Cymraeg i Ffoaduriaid (pp. 136–141), own sentence

karty.priklad: Mae mwy o bobl wedi bwcio gwestai glan môr nag erioed, meddai llefarydd ar ran y Bwrdd Croeso.
karty.priklad_cs: More people than ever have booked seaside hotels, said a spokesperson for the Tourist Board (pobl → [b]obl after o).
karty.mnemo: llefaru (to utter, to speak) + -ydd: the one who speaks – breath steaming in the freezing air.

extra.rod_pozn: grammatically masculine even for a woman
extra.pozn: llafar = spoken (L12); sentence from the news on p. 140, adapted

karty.priklad: Cafodd y lleidr ei arestio.
karty.priklad_cs: The thief was arrested.
karty.mnemo: The thief climbs a LADDER (LLEIDR) to the window, in a blue balaclava.

extra.pozn: from Latin latro; lladrad = burglary (L14); dwyn = to steal; own example

karty.priklad: Mae llawer o bobl wedi colli eu cartrefi mewn llifogydd.
karty.priklad_cs: Many people have lost their homes in floods.
karty.mnemo: Autumn LEAVES (LLIF) swept away on an ice-cold flood.

extra.pozn: usually in the plural llifogydd; llifo = to flow (L15), gorlifo = to overflow; sentence based on the news item on p. 140

karty.priklad: Mae'r tân wedi ei ddiffodd erbyn hyn, ond mae mwg du trwchus yn dod o'r ffatri o hyd.
karty.priklad_cs: The fire has been put out by now, but thick black smoke is still coming from the factory (diffodd → [dd]iffodd after ei = its).
karty.mnemo: Like English MUG: blue smoke curling up from a mug of tea outside on a freezing morning.

extra.pozn: ysmygu = to smoke; mwgwd (L9) only as a memory aid; sentence from the news on p. 140

karty.priklad: Dilynwch y patrwm.
karty.priklad_cs: Follow the pattern.
karty.mnemo: From English pattern: the pattern on a snowflake.

extra.pozn: a pattern in an exercise and a pattern on fabric; sentence from p. 134

karty.priklad: Roedd bywydau'r pysgotwyr mewn perygl.
karty.priklad_cs: The fishermen's lives were in danger.
karty.mnemo: Like English PERIL (both from Latin periculum): danger – an avalanche thundering down the slope.

extra.pozn: mewn perygl = in danger; peryglus = dangerous; own example

karty.priklad: Cafodd y pysgotwyr eu hachub gan y bad achub.
karty.priklad_cs: The fishermen were rescued by the lifeboat (achub → [h]achub after eu).
karty.mnemo: pysgod (fish) + -wr (the one who does it): a fisherman fishing through a hole in the ice.

extra.pozn: h after eu before a vowel: Help llaw, p. 142; bad achub (L4); own example

karty.priklad: Mae'r seiclwr Geraint Jones yn edrych ymlaen yn fawr at y Gemau Olympaidd ymhen dau fis.
karty.priklad_cs: The cyclist Geraint Jones is really looking forward to the Olympic Games in two months' time (mis → [f]is after dau; mawr → [f]awr after yn).
karty.mnemo: English cycle + -wr: a cyclist pedalling hard through the sleet.

extra.rod_pozn: grammatically masculine even for a woman
extra.pozn: synonym beiciwr (L20, separate card); sentence from the news on p. 140 (ymlaen added)

karty.priklad: Mae'r farchnad ar y sgwâr bob dydd Sadwrn.
karty.priklad_cs: The market is on the square every Saturday (marchnad → [f]archnad after y, feminine).
karty.mnemo: From English square: a Christmas ice rink in the town square.

extra.pozn: also an adjective: square; own example

karty.priklad: Bydd gormod o dir ffermio'n cael ei golli.
karty.priklad_cs: Too much farmland will be lost (tir → [d]ir after o; colli → [g]olli after ei = its).
karty.mnemo: TIR ~ Latin TERRA: land – here, the frozen tundra.

extra.pozn: tir ffermio = farmland; sentence from the dialogue on p. 137

karty.priklad: Mae car ail-law gyda fi.
karty.priklad_cs: I've got a second-hand car.
karty.mnemo: ail (second) + llaw (hand) = literally "second-hand", just like English.

extra.pozn: llaw → law after ail; the adjective doesn't change any further; own example

sever.priklad_cs: I've got a second-hand car (car → [g]ar after gen i).
sever.pozn: north: Mae gen i instead of Mae … gyda fi (L6)

karty.priklad: Mae ffenest gron yn yr eglwys.
karty.priklad_cs: There's a round window in the church (feminine form cron, soft-mutated after the feminine ffenest: crwn → [g]ron).
karty.mnemo: Sounds like CROWN: a crown is round.

extra.pozn: own example

karty.priklad: Aeth popeth yn esmwyth.
karty.priklad_cs: Everything went smoothly.
karty.mnemo: esMWYTH sounds like SMOOTH.

extra.pozn: own example

karty.priklad: Mae drych hirgrwn yn yr ystafell ymolchi.
karty.priklad_cs: There's an oval mirror in the bathroom.
karty.mnemo: hir (long) + crwn (round) = long-round: oval.

extra.pozn: crwn → grwn in the compound; the feminine form is outside the coursebook; own example

karty.priklad: Mae'r ystafell yn betryal.
karty.priklad_cs: The room is rectangular (petryal → [b]etryal after yn).
karty.mnemo: Reminds you of pedwar (four): the four corners of a rectangle.

extra.pozn: the book lists it among the adjectives, but it also means a rectangle; own example

karty.priklad: Roedd hi'n gwisgo ffrog smotiog.
karty.priklad_cs: She was wearing a spotty dress.
karty.mnemo: SPOT → smot + -iog: spotty.

extra.pozn: smotyn = spot, dot; s- does not mutate after the feminine ffrog; own example

karty.priklad: Gwisgodd Dafydd grys streipiog.
karty.priklad_cs: Dafydd put on a striped shirt (crys → [g]rys as the object after the verb form).
karty.mnemo: English stripe + -iog.

extra.pozn: streipen = stripe; own example
